Unit 01

Computer Components

A computer isn't one thing — it's a team of specialized parts working together.

DEFINITION
Components

The individual physical parts that make up a computer system. Each component has a specific job. Together they allow the computer to receive input, process data, store information, and produce output.

⚡
Key idea: Every single component is either Internal (inside the case) or External (outside the case). That's the first big split.
INTERNAL

Inside the Case

Parts that process, store, and manage data. You don't touch them directly — they work behind the scenes.

Examples: CPU, GPU, RAM, Motherboard, Storage, Power Supply, Cooling
EXTERNAL

Outside the Case

Parts you interact with directly. They give the computer input or receive output from it.

Examples: Keyboard, Mouse, Monitor, Webcam, Speakers, Printer
THE BIG PICTURE

What does a computer actually do?

  • Receive Input — a user sends data into the computer (typing, clicking, speaking)
  • Process Data — the CPU and GPU work on the data
  • Store Information — RAM holds it short-term; storage holds it long-term
  • Produce Output — results appear on screen, through speakers, or on paper

Click each step as you read it ↑

Unit 02

External Components

Parts outside the computer case that let you interact with it. They're split into two jobs: Input (you → computer) and Output (computer → you).

ALSO EXTERNAL

Case / Tower

The physical shell that supports and protects all the internal components. It's external, but its job is to house everything inside.

INPUT DEVICES — you send data IN
OUTPUT DEVICES — computer sends data OUT
👆
Hover or tap a card to flip it and see the definition. Some devices can be both input AND output (like a touchscreen).
Unit 03

Internal Components

The parts inside the case that make the computer actually work. Each one has a specific role — none of them are interchangeable.

DEEP DIVE

CPU vs. GPU — What's the difference?

CPU
Central Processing Unit
  • General-purpose processor
  • Handles most tasks & instructions
  • Great at a few complex tasks at once
  • Running apps, OS, logic, math
VS
GPU
Graphics Processing Unit
  • Specialized for graphics & visuals
  • Handles rendering & animations
  • Great at thousands of small tasks at once
  • Gaming, video editing, AI/ML
🎯
Simple way to remember: The CPU is the Swiss Army knife — good at everything. The GPU is the specialist — incredibly fast at one type of task (visuals and parallel work).
ANALOGY

RAM is like a Whiteboard

RAM
Short-term memory. Stores data the computer is actively using right now so it can be accessed instantly.
🪟
Whiteboard
You can quickly write, erase, and change things — but when you wipe it (or turn off the computer), everything is gone.

More RAM = more things open at once without the computer slowing down.

STORAGE

HDD vs. SSD

Hard Drive (HDD)
Uses spinning magnetic disks to save data permanently. Slower, but usually more storage for the price.
Moving parts
Solid State Drive (SSD)
Uses flash memory — no moving parts. Much faster than an HDD. More durable and quieter.
No moving parts
💡
Remember: RAM is temporary memory (gone when you shut down). Storage is permanent memory (stays when you turn off).
Unit 04

Ports & Connections

Connection points on a computer where you plug in cables or devices to transfer data, power, or signals.

THE 4 MAIN PORTS
PortWhat It DoesType
🖥️HDMI Connects computer to monitor — transfers video and audio only VIDEO + AUDIO
🌐Ethernet Connects the computer to the internet via a physical cable NETWORK
🔌USB-A Connects devices to transfer data only (the rectangular one) DATA
⚡USB-C Connects devices to share audio, video, and data — newer, oval shape DATA + VIDEO + AUDIO
